newsitem.title: spain: TENNIS-RIOS TUMBLES OUT BUT MOYA RECOVERS CLAY FORM.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-RIOS TUMBLES OUT BUT MOYA RECOVERS CLAY FORM.

text.p: Albert Portas delighted home fans by ousting last year's beaten finalist Marcelo Rios as the big names continued to tumble in the Barcelona Open tennis tournament on Wednesday.

Portas won the second round match 7-5 7-6, but another local favourite, Carlos Moya, bucked a trend that had seen eight seeds fall in the first two days to avenge a recent defeat by compatriot Francisco Clavet.
Chile's Rios was unable to cope with the tremendous power of the unheralded Portas, who came back from 4-1 down and saved three set points to take the first set.
The world number nine was at times outmanouevered by Portas, who has slipped to 133 in the rankings after missing much of last season with a knee injury.
Rios' resistance ended after a tremendous tussle in the second set when he netted an easy forehand put-away at 2-2 in the tie-break.
"In the tie-break I was right at the limit, to be honest. I don't know quite what happened, if he played badly, or if he was uncomfortable with my play," said Portas.
Portas faces another unfancied Spaniard, Fernando Vicente, in the third round, with a quarter-final place at stake against either Christian Ruud or Karim Alami, both unseeded.
Moya, seeded fourth, remains on course for a repeat of last year's semifinal with defending champion Thomas Muster of Austria, who needed three sets to beat Renzo Furlan of Italy on Tuesday.
Moya's 6-4 6-4 win came just a week after losing to Clavet in Estoril, where the Australian Open finalist had been unexpectedly out-of-sorts on his preferred, clay surface.
"I don't know what happened to me last week ... I've been doing morning and afternoon training sessions since then," said Moya, who admitted to having fitness problems.
Clavet, the losing finalist in Estoril, failed to take his only opportunity after breaking Moya early in the second set.
The Spanish number one took consecutive breaks after eliminating his backhand errors and mixing some outstanding lobs and drop shots into his baseline game.
"I'm pleased not for the result, but for the way I played," said Moya, who added his confidence had been affected by the defeat in Estoril and Spain's surprise Davis Cup elimination by Italy.
"Since the Australian Open, I've only really felt good in one game, and I lost some fitness on the American Tour," he said.
The most significant obstacle in Moya's path to the semifinals could be Andrei Medvedev.
The Ukranian followed Tuesday's victory over Estoril winner Alex Corretja with a comprehensive 6-2 6-0 win over another Spaniard, Carlos Costa.
In the bottom half of the draw local players Felix Mantilla and Alberto Berasategui will face each other thanks to straight-sets wins over Francis Roig and Australian Richard Fromberg respectively.
Albert Costa will add to a strong Spanish presence in the next round after beating Joan Albert Viloca 6-4 6-3.
